{"self_assessment": "Impact: I kept the table supplied so the builders never had to stop. I made four full 40-domino fetches for the shared bin, at 0:45, 2:00, 3:00 and 4:00, so the body and tail were built without anyone waiting on dominoes. The 143-domino fish outline was fully connected at the push.

Execution: After the supply runs I moved to inspecting and finishing. I inspected the lower fork several times, stood one fallen domino back up, laid five dominoes to carry the lower fork past its end and curl it up round the tail, and then stood one more back up to close the last break near the tip. By the end the whole run was connected from the start domino, tail included. I stopped fetching once the table had enough, and I kept hands off after that so nothing got bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I told the table early that I would keep the bin stocked, and I did. I let Maya know about the small break on the upper lobe. I coordinated with Priya and Tom on the lower fork, told them when I had already nudged the break, and agreed to a hands-off rule before the push to avoid bumps.

Leadership: I took ownership of the supply role and the lower fork finish without being asked. I flagged problems early and cleared up the status of the tail so the table could stop touching it. That kept the table focused and calm in the last minutes.

Overall, I believe the supply runs and the tail finish were a central part of getting a complete, connected fish to the push. I estimate my share of the table's result at about 30 percent.", "my_share_percent": 30}
